author: Anonymous
date: late first or early second century CE
addressee: Christian communities, addressed as 'children' and as a congregation
occasion: A community manual for instructing new Christians and ordering community life: moral teaching, baptism, fasting, prayer, Eucharist, and treatment of traveling teachers and prophets.
argument: The work opens with the Two Ways: a way of life and a way of death, and urges the reader to follow the way of life by loving God and neighbor and obeying commandments. It then gives instructions for baptism, fasting and prayer (including the Lord's Prayer three times daily), and the Eucharist with set prayers. It offers rules for receiving and testing apostles, prophets, and teachers, and for supporting true prophets with first fruits. It closes with instructions to appoint bishops and deacons, to practice mutual correction, and to stay watchful for the Lord's coming amid the final tribulation.

outline.move: The way of life is presented, beginning with love of God and neighbor, the golden rule, and continuing through commandments and virtues.
The way of death is described as a catalogue of vices and sins.
The reader is warned not to be led astray and is told to bear as much of the Lord's yoke as possible, especially avoiding food offered to idols.
Baptism is prescribed in the name of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, preferably in living water, with fasting beforehand.
Fasting is set on Wednesday and Friday rather than with the hypocrites, and the Lord's Prayer is to be prayed three times daily.
Eucharistic prayers over the cup and the broken bread are given, and participation is restricted to the baptized.
A post-communion thanksgiving is given, followed by acclamations and permission for prophets to give thanks freely.
Rules are given for receiving apostles (one day, no money) and for testing prophets (by behavior, not by spirit), with tests for false prophets.
Rules are given for receiving travelers: help passersby briefly; craftsmen who stay must work; those without craft are supported by the community; those who refuse to work are Christ-traffickers.
True prophets and teachers are to be supported, and first fruits are to be given to the prophets or to the poor.
The community is to gather on the Lord's day, confess sins, be reconciled, and offer a pure sacrifice.
Bishops and deacons are to be appointed, and mutual correction is to be done peacefully according to the gospel.

The community is urged to watch and be ready, for in the last days false prophets and destroyers will multiply, love will turn to hatred, the world-deceiver will appear performing signs, and finally the Lord will come.

cast.name: The Lord
cast.who: Jesus Christ, whose commands and gospel are cited as authoritative.

cast.name: Apostles
cast.who: Traveling emissaries who are to be received but tested.

cast.name: Prophets
cast.who: Spirit-inspired teachers who may settle and are supported by first fruits.

cast.name: Teachers
cast.who: Instructors who, like prophets, are worthy of support.

cast.name: Bishops
cast.who: Local leaders to be appointed by the community.

cast.name: Deacons
cast.who: Local ministers to be appointed alongside bishops.

cast.name: False prophets
cast.who: Deceivers who must be tested and rejected.

cast.name: The world-deceiver
cast.who: An end-time figure who will appear as a son of God and perform signs.

scripture: The author cites the gospel and the Lord's Prayer in forms close to Matthew, and quotes material resembling Malachi 1:11 and/or 1:14 in section 14, though the exact textual source is debated. Psalm numbering follows the Septuagint where applicable; modern citations should use standard English Bible book names and Psalm numbering.
uncertain: The exact date and place of composition are uncertain.
The identity of the author is unknown.
The precise relationship between the Didache's prayers and later eucharistic liturgies is debated.
The meaning of 'the first fruits' in section 13 as applied to money and clothing is not fully specified.
The exact source of the quotation in section 14 resembling Malachi 1:11 and/or 1:14 is debated.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Teachers — Instructors who, like prophets, are worthy of support.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὡσαύτως διδάσκαλος ἀληθινός ἐστιν ἄξιος καὶ αὐτὸς ὥσπερ ὁ ἐργάτης τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Teachers — Instructors who, like workers, are worthy of their food (not explicitly grouped with prophets for first fruits; only prophets receive first fruits in section 13)

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: καὶ γὰρ περὶ τούτου εἴρηκεν ὁ κύριος: Μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἄγιον τοῖς κυσίν
_unresolved_facts.fix: sections: ["9"] — The Lord is explicitly quoted only in section 9 ('the Lord said'). Section 8 cites 'as the Lord commanded in his gospel' but does not quote direct speech marked as from the Lord. Section 14 quotes 'the Lord said' regarding pure sacrifice, so ["9", "14"]

sections: ["8", "9", "10"] — but note: the Lord's Prayer in section 8 is presented as 'as the Lord commanded in his gospel, so pray' — it is the Lord's Prayer, not a community-composed prayer. Sections 9 and 10 contain eucharistic prayers spoken by the community.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Christ (Χριστοῦ) — appears once in section 9 only
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας
_unresolved_facts.fix: Christ (Χριστοῦ) — appears in section 9 only, but the brief should note this is the only occurrence of the full title 'Jesus Christ' in the work

_unresolved_facts.claim: sections ["11"]: 'Rules are given for receiving apostles (one day, no money) and for testing prophets (by behavior, not by spirit), with tests for false prophets.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Καὶ πάντα προφήτην λαλοῦντα ἐν πνεύματι οὐ πειράσετε οὐδὲ διακρινεῖτε
_unresolved_facts.fix: Rules are given for receiving apostles (one or two days, no money) and for testing prophets (by behavior, not by testing the spirit itself), with tests for false prophets. Note: prophets speaking in spirit are not to be tested or judged, but their behavior reveals them.

_unresolved_facts.claim: sections ["12"]: 'those without craft are supported by the community'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: εἰ δὲ οὐκ ἔχει τέχνην, κατὰ τὴν σύνεσιν ὑμῶν προνοήσατε, πῶς μὴ ἀργὸς μεθ̓ ὑμῶν ζήσεται Χριστιανός
_unresolved_facts.fix: those without craft are to be provided for by the community according to their understanding, so that the Christian does not live idle among them

_unresolved_facts.claim: sections ["16"]: 'the world-deceiver will appear performing signs'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ποιήσει σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα, καὶ ἡ γῆ παραδοθήσεται εἰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ, καὶ ποιήσει ἀθέμιτα, ἅ οὐδέποτε γέγονεν ἐξ αἰῶνος
_unresolved_facts.fix: the world-deceiver will appear as a son of God, performing signs and wonders, and the earth will be delivered into his hands, and he will do unlawful things never done from eternity
